items.title: Oral and Fecal Microbial Dysbiosis as Non-Invasive Diagnostic Biomarkers for Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including esophageal (EC), gastric (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), impose a substantial global burden, with early detection remaining crucial for improving patient outcomes. The oral and gut microbiota are increasingly implicated in cancer development and hold promise as sources of non-invasive biomarkers. However, current evidence on microbiome-based diagnostics remains fragmented, and a systematic comparison of the diagnostic accuracy between oral and fecal sampling across multiple GI cancer types is lacking. To address this gap, a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus up to December 31, 2025, identified 43 case-control studies (59 cohorts) comprising 4452 cancer patients and 5809 controls. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.846 (95% CI: 0.824-0.867), though with substantial heterogeneity (I 2  = 86.5%). By cancer type, pooled AUCs were 0.746 for EC (5 cohorts), 0.886 for GC (8 cohorts), and 0.850 for CRC (46 cohorts). A bivariate analysis of 20 cohorts comparing sample types found no statistically significant difference in diagnostic performance between oral (sAUC = 0.863) and fecal sampling (sAUC = 0.820; p = 0.369). While these exploratory findings suggest that oral and fecal microbial biomarkers may offer comparable diagnostic accuracy for GI cancers, with oral sampling presenting a more practical option for screening, the results are preliminary. Significant heterogeneity, a limited number of oral cohorts, and the absence of clinical control groups highlight the need for large-scale prospective studies with direct comparisons and real-world validation to validate these biomarkers for clinical translation.

items.title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on the Prognosis and Emergency Treatment of Patients with Ischemic Stroke in Suzhou, China: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted stroke care globally. This study aimed to assess the impact of COVID-19 on the clinical characteristics, acute treatment, and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in Suzhou, China. This study retrospectively analyzed 506 hospitalized AIS patients from four stroke centers between December 10, 2022, and January 20, 2023. Patients were grouped by COVID- 19 infection status and timing. Clinical data and outcomes were compared with a pre-pandemic cohort from the SUMMITS-II Study. Among included AIS patients, 54.3% were COVID-19-positive. Infected patients had higher baseline NIHSS scores, elevated inflammatory markers, and more in-hospital complications. Intravenous thrombolysis rates increased slightly during the pandemic, despite longer prehospital delays. Emotional disorders were more frequent post-stroke. COVID-19 infection, particularly concurrent with stroke onset, was linked to worse outcomes at 90 days and 1 year. The findings suggest that the COVID-19 pandemic significantly influenced the clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with acute ischemic stroke in Suzhou. Patients with AIS with concomitant COVID-19 infection presented with a higher prevalence of vascular risk factors and elevated inflammatory and coagulation markers. Moreover, COVID-19 infection occurring within one week of stroke onset was associated with more severe neurological deficits and poorer short- and long-term prognosis, highlighting the potential role of COVID-19 in worsening stroke outcomes. The COVID-19 pandemic adversely affected stroke severity and prognosis. While in-hospital workflows were preserved, delayed presentation and increased systemic burden contributed to unfavorable stroke outcomes. Strengthening stroke care delivery and psychological support during public health crises is essential.

items.title: Endovascular versus open repair for aortoiliac occlusive disease - nationwide in-hospital outcomes by sex.
items.abstract: Background: Evidence comparing endovascular therapy and open surgery for aorto-iliac occlusive disease remains limited, particularly for early complications, resource use, and sex-specific outcomes. Patients and methods: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the 2023 German inpatient dataset. Adult hospitalisations with major endovascular or open aorto-iliac reconstructive procedures and arterial occlusive disease were included. Hospitalisations with aneurysm, dissection, or combined procedure codes were excluded. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), complications, length of stay, and reimbursement. Adjusted estimates were obtained employing a doubly robust estimator using machine learning algorithms and were stratified by sex. Results: Among 2,710 hospitalisations, 1,923 (71.0%) underwent open surgery and 787 (29.0%) endovascular therapy; 41.3% involved women. Endovascular therapy was associated with lower adjusted risks of in-hospital mortality (RR .44, 95% CI .31-.64), MACCE (RR .47, 95% CI .34-.64), acute kidney injury (RR .38, 95% CI .29-.50), major bleeding (RR .36, 95% CI .25-.51), prolonged ventilation (RR .28, 95% CI .18-.43), and SAEs (RR .46, 95% CI .33-.65). Length of stay was shorter after endovascular therapy (-8.57 days, 95% CI -9.63 to -7.52), while reimbursement did not differ significantly. Sex-stratified estimates were more pronounced in men but exploratory without interaction testing. Conclusions : Endovascular therapy was associated with lower in-hospital morbidity and mortality and shorter hospital stay than open surgery, with similar reimbursement. Case-based data lacked longitudinal follow-up and detailed clinical, anatomical and treatment-selection information, limiting causal and patient-level interpretation.

MAFG as a Redox-Sensitive Node Linking Peripheral Immune Reprogramming to Cognitive Risk in the Sepsis-to-Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: Single-Cell Dissection and Adoptive-Transfer Validation.
items.abstract: Sepsis survivors face an elevated long-term risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the peripheral pathways linking systemic immune activation to chronic neurodegeneration remain undefined. We mapped peripheral immune reprogramming across sepsis and AD and tested a candidate regulatory node. A single-cell atlas of peripheral immunity was built by integrating scRNA-seq from human sepsis and AD cohorts, using clustering, SCENIC regulatory-network inference and an exploratory pseudotime ordering. The resulting signature was validated in two clinical cohorts (ROC and survival analysis). MAFG-associated subpopulations and redox status were profiled in APP/PS1, cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) and composite models, and causality was tested by lentiviral MAFG knockdown and adoptive transfer into APP/PS1 recipients. Peripheral immunity was myeloid-skewed in sepsis and lymphoid-dominated in AD, with APP-expressing common myeloid progenitors (CMPs), dendritic cells (DCs), and platelets forming an APP-enriched compartment. A core transcription-factor network differed between disease states, yielding a four-gene signature (MAFG, NFIL3, RGS10, FOXO3) with cross-cohort diagnostic and prognostic value. MAFG was upregulated in septic patients and associated with poorer survival, subpopulation expansion, and systemic oxidative stress. Superimposed CLP aggravated amyloid deposition, microglial activation, and memory deficits in APP/PS1 mice, whereas MAFG silencing restored Aβ uptake and, on adoptive transfer, reduced amyloid burden, attenuated microgliosis, and preserved cognition. Peripheral immune states differ across the sepsis-to-AD spectrum and are captured by a MAFG-centered signature. Independent of any trajectory assumption, loss-of-function and adoptive-transfer experiments identify MAFG as a causal, redox-sensitive node constraining peripheral Aβ clearance and a candidate biomarker and therapeutic target in sepsis survivors.

items.title: Oxygen-Amplified Carrier-Free Nanomedicine Integrating Ferroptosis/Photodynamic Therapy and COX-2/PGE2 Blockade for Robust Antitumor Immunity Against Glioma.
items.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of glioma immunotherapy is severely hampered by immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment. Here, we develop an oxygen‑amplified carrier‑free nanomedicine (IHC NPs) through hydrophobic self‑assembly of IR-820, hemin, and celecoxib. IHC NPs exhibit excellent stability, biological safety, and preferential tumor accumulation. In the subcutaneous glioma model, the combination of IHC NPs and αPD-L1 significantly inhibited subcutaneous tumor growth and effectively prevented distant tumor metastasis. Mechanistically, hemin catalyzes endogenous H2O2 to generate oxygen, thereby alleviating tumor hypoxia. This oxygen boost potentiates IR-820‑mediated photodynamic therapy and hemin-based ferroptosis, enhancing direct tumor cell killing. Concurrently, celecoxib blocks the COX‑2/PGE2 pathway, reversing immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment. Through the synergistic strategy combining oxygen-sensitized photodynamic therapy, ferroptosis, COX-2/PGE2 suppression, and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, this therapeutic regimen effectively induces tumor immunogenic cell death, promotes dendritic cell maturation, enhances intratumoral infiltration of cytotoxic T lymphocytes, reduces the abundance of regulatory T cells, and triggers the generation of effector memory T cells, thereby potently activating the host immune system. Collectively, our work provides a promising oxygen‑amplified carrier‑free nanomedicine for robust glioma immunotherapy.

items.title: Context-dependent TREM2 signalling in myeloid cells: Molecular mechanisms and immunotherapeutic divergence in neurodegeneration and cancer.
items.abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a pivotal lipid-sensing receptor that governs the functional plasticity and metabolic fitness of mononuclear phagocytes, including microglia, osteoclasts, dendritic cells and tissue-resident macrophages. While originally identified as a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), TREM2 functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic checkpoint rather than a uniform phenotypic driver, exerting divergent biological outputs dictated by distinct tissue microenvironments and ligand repertoires. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of TREM2 immunobiology, detailing how ligand engagement-including cell-surface phospholipids and apolipoprotein E (ApoE)-activates the DAP12/DAP10-SYK-PI3K-mTOR signalling axis. This coordinated intracellular cascade instructively drives myeloid adaptation towards metabolically competent disease-associated microglia (DAM) and lipid-associated macrophage (LAM) states, sustaining bioenergetics and debris clearance under pathological stress. Across neurodegenerative proteinopathies and acute cerebral ischemia, TREM2 signalling is predominantly neuroprotective by promoting aggregate compaction and mitigating secondary excitotoxicity, although chronic dysregulated activation may drive stage-dependent neuroinflammation. In peripheral inflammatory pathologies such as rheumatoid arthritis and sepsis, TREM2 fine-tunes macrophage efferocytosis and systemic metabolic thresholds. In oncology, TREM2 displays a complex, microenvironment-dependent divergence: in central nervous system malignancies such as glioblastoma (GBM), TREM2 exerts controversial, stage-dependent effects, spanning microglial tumour containment in early stages versus pro-tumoural myelin recycling and immunosuppression by monocyte-derived macrophages in post-treatment recurrence; conversely, in peripheral solid tumours, monocyte-derived TREM2+ tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) predominantly orchestrate an immunosuppressive, nutrient-deprived niche that impairs cytotoxic T-cell function. Furthermore, we synthesise emerging paradigms along the bidirectional microbiome-gut-brain-tumour axis, elucidating how commensal and intra-tumoural microbial cues dynamically calibrate myeloid signalling tone and therapeutic susceptibility. We address translation bottlenecks-including blood-brain barrier (BBB) shuttles, human trial scarcity and soluble TREM2 (sTREM2) biomarker harmonisation-outlining a biomarker-guided, context-tailored precision therapeutic framework for targeting the TREM2 axis.

items.title: JAK-STAT pathway heterogeneity governs immunotherapy response in breast cancer.
items.abstract: The JAK-STAT pathway (JSP) is a well-known oncogenic cascade; however, recent clinical trials have detected JSP upregulation in breast cancer following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. This paradoxical observation warrants further investigation into JSP's intercellular heterogeneity, tumor dynamics, molecular mechanisms, and clinical implications for immunotherapy. JSP expression showed dynamic shifts during breast cancer progression, with higher levels in T cells and paracancerous epithelial cells. In human breast cancer tumor cells, elevated JSP is highly correlated with malignant phenotypes. JSP-high tumor cells overexpressed oncogenic pathways, while exhibiting increased immunosuppressive signaling via the MIF-CD74 signaling axis. In T cells, higher JSP levels were associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved differentiation, and reduced exhaustion, reflecting robust anti-tumor immunity. Analysis of immunotherapy datasets revealed that higher JSP levels were associated with improved responses toward PD-1 inhibitors, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients, with JSP serving as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy sensitivity. As a key JSP component, STAT4 exerts dual roles in breast cancer: it drives tumorigenesis in malignant cells, sustains breast epithelial cell proliferation, and bolsters T-cell anti-tumor functionality, while also acting as a highly accurate biomarker for predicting immunotherapy response. This indicates that JSP targeting demands a nuanced approach: broad inhibition may impair anti-tumor immunity, and optimized therapeutic strategies paired with precise biomarkers are critical to maximize JSP's utility in breast cancer immunotherapy. Our findings highlight JSP's functional heterogeneity in epithelial, tumor, and T cells, with high JSP activity correlating with enhanced immunotherapy efficacy in breast cancer.

items.title: Nanomedicines for prostate cancer therapy: stimuli-responsive design and disease-specific applications.
items.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains a major malignancy among men and is clinically complicated by biological heterogeneity, treatment resistance and frequent bone metastasis. Current therapeutic strategies, including radical local treatment, androgen deprivation therapy, androgen receptor (AR) pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy and radioligand therapy, have improved disease control, but their efficacy is often limited by systemic toxicity, functional burden and insufficient tumour selectivity. Chemistry-enabled nanomedicines offer a versatile route to improve drug solubility, circulation, tumour accumulation and controlled therapeutic activation. In this review, we summarise recent advances in nanomedicines for PCa therapy with an emphasis on two closely related aspects: stimuli-responsive design and disease-specific applications. First, endogenous stimuli-responsive drug delivery systems are discussed, including platforms activated by acidic pH, hypoxia, redox imbalance and aberrant enzyme activity. Exogenous systems regulated by light, ultrasound and magnetic fields are then reviewed, with attention to how carrier architecture, responsive linkers, surface transformation and externally triggered activation influence payload release and therapeutic output. Second, PCa-specific nanoplatforms are highlighted, focusing on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-directed delivery, AR axis- and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC)-oriented intervention, and bone metastasis-adapted design. Nanomedicine-enabled combinations with immunotherapy or radiotherapy are also considered. Finally, we discuss key challenges related to tumour delivery efficiency, structural complexity, manufacturing reproducibility, biosafety and patient stratification. Overall, this review highlights how rational chemical design can be integrated with prostate cancer biology to develop more precise and clinically translatable nanotherapy strategies.

items.title: Superior Efficacy of Besifovir in Reducing Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Compared to Tenofovir in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Besifovir dipivoxil maleate (BSV) is a novel therapeutic option for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its long-term effectiveness in reducing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database from 2018 to 2022. A total of 32,383 patients with CHB were included (BSV, n = 2,358; tenofovir disoproxil fumarate [TDF], n = 30,025). Propensity score matching was conducted at a 1:3 ratio to minimize selection bias. The primary outcome was the incidence of HCC, with cirrhosis development as the secondary endpoint. In the overall population, 57 cases of HCC were reported in the BSV group (2,358 individuals, 5,918 person-years), while 1,268 cases of HCC were reported in the TDF group (30,025 individuals, 83,587 person-years). After propensity score matching, the incidence of HCC was significantly lower in the BSV group (9.63 per 1,000 person-years; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.43-12.49) than in the TDF group (15.36 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI, 13.72-17.18), with an incidence rate ratio of 1.59 ( P = 0.001). This protective effect remained consistent in both cirrhotic (hazard ratio [HR], 1.609; P = 0.028) and non-cirrhotic subgroups (HR, 1.831; P = 0.002). BSV treatment demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing the risk of HCC compared to TDF, regardless of baseline cirrhosis status. These findings suggest that BSV may provide enhanced protection against HCC in patients with CHB.

items.title: Pathophysiology and Pharmacological Management of Chronic Liver Injury: Current Challenges and Future Directions.
items.abstract: Chronic liver injury results from persistent hepatic injuries such as metabolic disorders, alcohol consumption, viral infections, drug toxicity, autoimmune conditions, and genetic factors. It is a major global health concern due to its progression to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. This review aims to summarize key pathophysiological mechanisms and evaluate current and emerging pharmacological strategies. A narrative review of preclinical and clinical studies was conducted, focusing on inflammation, oxidative stress, immune dysfunction, fibrogenesis, and therapeutic approaches, including conventional drugs, antifibrotics, metabolic modulators, and advanced drug delivery systems. A total of 352 records were identified, of which 158 studies were included in the review. Chronic liver injury is characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, hepatocyte death, impaired regeneration, and activation of hepatic stellate cells, leading to extracellular matrix accumulation and fibrosis. Current therapies are largely etiology-based and slow disease progression but rarely reverse fibrosis. Emerging therapies targeting nuclear receptors, metabolic pathways, gene-based interventions, microbiome modulation, and nanocarrier-based systems show promising potential. These findings indicate that chronic liver injury is a complex, multifactorial process involving interconnected molecular pathways, limiting the effectiveness of single-target therapies. The gap between mechanistic insights and clinical translation remains a key challenge. Multi-targeted, combination, and precision-based therapeutic approaches, along with targeted drug delivery systems, may enhance treatment efficacy and overcome current limitations. Despite advances in understanding disease mechanisms, effective diseasemodifying therapies remain limited. The development of combination and personalized treatment strategies is essential for improving outcomes and preventing disease progression.

items.title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST-HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double-Blind Phase IIa Study.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template-covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)-and the need for lifelong treatment. GST-HG131 is a first-in-class, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST-HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study. This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST-HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 (n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 (n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were -0.65 log 10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28-day group and -0.53 log 10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28-day group. The 30 mg BID 12-week group showed a greater reduction of -0.89 log 10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo (p   50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log 10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12-week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST-HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose-related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. GST-HG131, a first-in-class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST-HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959. Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health challenge because current antiviral therapies rarely achieve a functional cure, mainly due to the persistence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and stable viral templates in infected liver cells. This study evaluated GST‐HG131, an oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, in patients with CHB receiving stable nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. Treatment with GST‐HG131 resulted in significant reductions in HBsAg levels, with the greatest effect observed after 12 weeks of treatment. The treatment was safe and generally well tolerated. These findings suggest that GST‐HG131 may represent a promising therapeutic approach to enhance functional cure rates for patients with CHB.

items.title: Evaluating the potential of treatment options for chronic hepatitis B.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide, but long-term or even lifelong viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) seldom clears hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), so-called 'functional cure.' In recent years, a shift in treatment strategy from viral suppression toward cure has emerged, catalyzed by three revised international hepatitis B guidelines (2025-2026) and the first-in-class phase 3 evidence that a finite antiviral therapy, the antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen, can achieve a functional cure in about one in five NA-suppressed CHB patients with baseline HBsAg below 3000 IU/mL. We evaluated the spectrum of established and emerging treatment options for CHB, organized around quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) as the axis for selecting and sequencing therapy. Coverage spans backbone NAs and pegylated interferon-α, an HBsAg-guided roadmap, finite NA therapy and off-treatment outcomes, bepirovirsen, other virus-targeting and immunomodulatory agents, and genome-directed covalently closed circular DNA silencing and editing. Bepirovirsen's approaching approval is an inflection point. qHBsAg should guide personalized, sequential therapy, with partial cure (HBsAg < 100 IU/mL) as a potential intermediate target when functional cure is unlikely. Durability, standardized biomarkers, rational combination design, metabolic co-management and equitable access are the priorities; a sterilizing cure remains distant.

items.title: The long noncoding RNA MAPKAPK5-AS1 promotes the formation of hepatitis B virus cccDNA by modulating the expression of NABP1.
items.abstract: Cellular long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown to participate in diverse biological pathways, including the regulation of virus infections. However, their functions in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) life cycle still need to be explored. Here, we conducted a loss-of-function screen targeting 1779 human lncRNAs and identified 19 lncRNAs associated with HBV infection. One lncRNA, named MAPKAPK5-AS1 (lnc-MAAS), was identified as a host factor required for HBV infection. Our data suggest that lnc-MAAS is involved in the conversion of HBV relaxed circular DNA into covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA). Furthermore, mechanistic experiments revealed that lnc-MAAS affects cccDNA formation by modulating the expression of nucleic acid binding protein 1 (NABP1). Together, our findings shed light on the roles of host lnc-MAAS and NABP1 in HBV cccDNA formation, which may contribute to the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics.

items.title: Exploring Structure-Activity Relationships: Discovering the Anticancer Potential of Dietary Bioactive Constituents: A Mini-Review.
items.abstract: Cancer is the leading cause of mortality worldwide. It encompasses a spectrum of malignancies that include lung, stomach, colon, prostate, liver, and skin cancers depending on the organ it affects. Epidemiological evidence indicates that regular consumption of cruciferous vegetables leads to a 10-20% reduction in the risk of lung, breast, and colorectal cancers and bioactive dietary constituents. The lipophilic character of phytochemicals facilitates membrane permeability and selective target engagement, underscoring their pharmacological relevance. Daily dietary intake introduces varying amounts of bioactive constituents that can act as preventive agents, thereby improving human health. In this review, we discuss the therapeutic potential of selected dietary natural products, focusing on cinnamaldehyde, eugenol, β-glucan, gingerol, shogaol, curcumin, and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Strong scientific literature studies support the role of these compounds in targeting key molecular pathways, including the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, caspase-3 activation, and Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) signaling. Bioavailability, dosing, and safety profiles remain challenges, particularly in ensuring that these factors do not hinder therapeutic efficacy. Analyzing the pharmacophoric features and discussing their potential for structural optimization leads to the development of clinical candidates in the market. Combination therapy of plant-derived bioactive compounds with anticancer drugs has improved patient outcomes in many studies, leading to the development of natural product-assisted therapeutics in the future.

items.title: Tumor Biology and Surgical Margin Patterns in Colorectal Liver Metastases: Association Between KRAS/BRAF Status and Type of Resection Margin-BRAF-KRAS LiverMet Collaborative Group .
items.abstract: Surgical strategies for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) have progressively evolved toward parenchyma-sparing approaches, increasing the relevance of understanding the relationship between tumor biology and resection margin patterns. In parallel, KRAS and BRAF mutations have emerged as key determinants of tumor behavior in CRLM. The interaction between mutational status and surgical margin type, however, remains insufficiently characterized. This multicenter retrospective study included patients undergoing curative-intent liver resection for CRLM between 2016 and 2021 across 17 international HPB centers. Clinicopathological variables were compared according to mutational status and margin type. Among 1078 eligible patients, KRAS-mutated patients more frequently presented synchronous metastases, nodal involvement, and administration of perioperative chemotherapy compared with wild-type patients. Higher tumor burden was associated with both R1 parenchymal (R1P) and R1 vascular (R1V) resections. Within KRAS-mutated patients, synchronous disease and bilobar involvement were more frequently associated with R1P resections. KRAS/BRAF mutational status is associated with distinct clinicopathological patterns in patients undergoing liver resection for CRLM. Higher tumor burden and biologically aggressive disease features are more frequently associated with R1P and R1V resections, particularly among KRAS-mutated tumors.

items.title: First Unscheduled Hospitalization in Pancreatic Cancer: A Point for Palliative Care Integration.
items.abstract: Pancreatic cancer is characterized by high symptom burden, rapid deterioration, and poor survival. Despite this complexity, specialist palliative care (SPC) is often integrated late or not at all. The first unscheduled hospitalization may represent a point for SPC assessment. To characterize frequency, clinical features, and outcomes of the first unscheduled hospitalization in pancreatic adenocarcinoma, explore factors associated with subsequent survival, and describe the timing of SPC assessment. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adults with pancreatic adenocarcinoma managed by medical oncology at three tertiary hospitals during 2022-2023, with follow-up through 2025. Overall survival (OS) from hospitalization was estimated with Kaplan-Meier methods; univariable Cox regression assessed associations with survival. Among 125 patients, 105 (84%) experienced a first unscheduled hospitalization at a median of 4.1 months after diagnosis (IQR, 1.9-8.0). Median OS was 3.8 months (95% CI, 2.1-7.1); 21/104 (20%) died in hospital, and 62/80 (78%) were readmitted after discharge. ECOG performance status 2-4 (HR, 3.30), metastatic disease (HR, 3.05), liver metastases (HR, 2.58), and strong opioid use (HR, 2.10) were associated with shorter survival. Only 11 (10%) underwent SPC assessment before hospitalization; 31 (30%) were first assessed during hospitalization, 40 (38%) afterward, and 23 (22%) remained unassessed. A first unscheduled hospitalization occurred in most patients, marking limited survival, high in-hospital mortality, and frequent readmission. Most lacked prior SPC assessment. This event may serve as a pragmatic safety net for palliative care integration, complementing earlier needs- and prognosis-based referral strategies.
items.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management

items.title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of macroregenerative and high-grade dysplastic nodules in cirrhotic liver: A pilot study.
items.abstract: High-grade dysplastic nodules (HGDN) are recognized precursors of hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis, yet their distinction from macro-regenerative nodules (MRN) relies entirely on morphologic features that exist along a continuum rather than as discrete thresholds, with no ancillary marker available to adjudicate this boundary. Whether these lesions represent distinct molecular states remains unknown. We performed whole-transcriptome spatial profiling (GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler, Bruker) of MRN and HGDN within their native cirrhotic microenvironment in FFPE explant specimens from three patients. Fifteen regions of interest spanning background cirrhosis (n = 2), MRN (n = 3), HGDN (n = 4), and the HGDN-cirrhotic interface (n = 6) underwent exploratory differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses; because MRN and HGDN derived from different patients, lesion class and donor could not be separated. MRN showed a quiescent regenerative program characterized by HGFAC upregulation, depletion of inflammatory and immunoglobulin transcripts, and no significant upregulation of canonical hepatocellular carcinoma markers. HGDN showed PZP, DEPP1, and CDHR5 upregulation and enrichment of interferon signaling. Spatially, HGDN separated into a metallothionein-enriched core and an MHC-I/interferon-enriched interface expressing HLA-B, HLA-C, and IFI6, a pattern that bulk profiling would be expected to obscure; the core-interface distinction persisted when analysis was restricted to a single patient. In this pilot cohort, morphologically defined regenerative and premalignant hepatocellular nodules showed distinct transcriptional profiles, providing preliminary, hypothesis-generating molecular support for a difficult morphologic distinction. These observations, including the MHC-I/interferon-enriched dysplastic interface, identify candidate targets for validation in larger cohorts with paired lesions.
